summary: No trades today, and no proposals reached me. The account closed at $617.91 (+$1.97 on the day, +2.99% since inception against SPY's -6.50%), 50.5% invested against the shadow's 88.1%. The shadow gained about 1.0% today to our 0.35% while SPY fell 0.29%. That is one holiday-week session and doesn't grade anything. No stop_alerts, and every stop block reads ok at the close. TLT is now the closest at 7.79% above $76.30, then DPZ at 7.92% above its raised $335 stop and SAM at 8.22% above $201 after a 2.7% bounce. No stored qualitative clause was met: KR's cyber matter is still unconfirmed and its guidance clause waits for the 12-03 call; SAM and the Health Care names have no guidance-cut 8-K; TLT rose 0.86% while SPY fell, so its duration clause is not in play. Given the regime filter, the empty trade list was right. The only allowed buys were TLT and GLD. TLT was at the target weight I stated (about 8%, L4), and GLD is on the Market Analyst's avoid list. I named the cash as idled by the filter, and I pre-stated a re-entry plan (about 75-80% invested within a week of the filter turning on, own-stop menu names in favored sectors first, 3-5% each), which the Skeptic asked for. The thesis_updates did what L6 and L8 asked. TLT's stop is restated from the $81.10 blended cost, and that figure checks out across the three lots. The false gain wording is gone from DPZ and IDXX, and their new text and stop_prices agree with the fill. IDXX's and INCY's stale sector lines are restated without leaning on the restored tilt. SAM is named the first sell candidate, so the Proposer owes a sale or a non-beta hold verdict. On KR I weighed the Skeptic's pre-print one-third trim and rejected it on its merits, under L10's partial-sale clause. I gave the size difference from WMT's 11-13 case and Staples' lead, and I dropped the negative-beta argument both theses disclaim. Weak points: (1) I said I accepted the Skeptic's DPZ concentration objection, but the only fix was a tighter stop, $335, about 6% under the mark. That changes the exit point, not the size. DPZ is still about 12% of equity, roughly a quarter of the invested book, and closed up another 1.5%. I neither named DPZ a trim candidate under L8 nor asked the Proposer for a trim proposal, so the accepted objection has no path to a trade. (2) TLT's stop is 0.6 sigma deep against a 12-09 FOMC with hikes priced, and long duration carries more of that event risk than intermediate. 'Hold through unless a clause trips' is a plan. It hasn't priced a gap through the stop on the decision day, which the Market Analyst flagged. (3) My re-entry plan depends on the filter turning on, and the Proposer has not named specific names or weights for it. If SPY reclaims its 200-day around the holiday, the first run could be improvised again.
lessons: When I accept a concentration objection (DPZ at about 12% of equity), a tighter stop is not the remedy, because it changes when we exit, not how much we hold. Name the position a trim candidate in thesis_updates under L8 so the Proposer owes a trim proposal or an explicit size-justified hold at the next run.

A pre-stated re-entry plan should name candidates and weights, not just a rule. Ask the Proposer to list the first three to five own-stop menu names with weights while the filter is off, so the run on which SPY reclaims its 200-day is not improvised (L9, L4).

Before a scheduled macro event that a position's own thesis names as its main risk (TLT and the 12-09 FOMC), say on the last run before it whether a close-based stop can protect the position from a gap. If it can't, weigh a partial trim then, as WMT was trimmed before its print. Don't leave the stored stop as the only protection.
